chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Misma' ibn Abdul-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the one in Ihram hunts a prey and hits two, then upon him are two expiations, their penalty.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram, a sacred ritual state for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim in Ihram who kills two animals while hunting?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of cumulative liability in Islamic jurisprudence, establishing that each animal hunted by a pilgrim in Ihram constitutes a distinct offense requiring a separate expiation (kaffarah). It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise legal quantification, ensuring that the penalty scales directly with the number of animals killed rather than being treated as a single incident. This ruling underscores the sanctity of the Haram boundaries and the specific restrictions placed upon the pilgrim's state of consecration.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the one in Ihraam pelts a prey, so he hits two, so upon him would be two expiations, as two penalties’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Misma’ ibn ‘Abd al-Malik who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a hunter in the state of Ihram shoots a prey and kills two of them, he owes Kaffarah (expiation) for two as penalty.’”
